openesm.participants: 18-40 year old people who play video games

original_licence.how: read LICENSE in github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play: CC0 1.0 plus a section 5 no-reidentification clause

licence_note: Licence: CC0 1.0 with an added no-reidentification clause (LICENSE in github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play, section 5): "Users must not attempt to reidentify, deanonymize, or otherwise link the data to specific individuals. This includes combining the dataset with other information sources for the purpose of reidentification." The clause also bars sharing derived data in a way that could enable reidentification. Cleared on #3421 (2026-11-15).
reference: Ballou, N., Földes, T. A., Vuorre, M., Hakman, T., Magnusson, K., & Przybylski, A. K. (2026). Open Play: A longitudinal dataset of multi-platform video game digital trace data and psychological measures (Version 2). PsyArXiv. https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/nz96c_v2

date.tz_evidence: Daily links went out at 2pm local time and stayed open until 3am (v2 preprint, 10.31234/osf.io/nz96c_v2). As written, US surveys start at 18h (2pm EDT) and run to about 07h, with almost none 08-13h; UK surveys start 13-16h (2pm BST/GMT). So the Z stamps are true UTC. Window: neither the v2 preprint, the open-play README nor CITATION.cff states the collection period, so the window is the data's own span (2024-10-01 18:54Z .. 2025-08-30 00:54Z), widened to whole days.

tables.name: ballou_2025_bangs
tables.instrument: Basic Needs in Games Scale (BANGS; Ballou & Deterding, 2024), 6-item daily version
tables.description: Daily diary (US participants, 30 days): six BANGS items about the participant's most recent gaming session, asked on days they had played in the previous 24 hours. 1 = strongly disagree .. 7 = strongly agree.
tables.dict_note: Sparse per person: the median person answers each item 7 times (interquartile range 2 to 19), because most people completed only a few of the 30 daily surveys and BANGS is asked only on days they had played. These are short diaries for most people, not a dense diary.

items.stem: In my most recent session of [game]... I could play in the way I wanted.
In my most recent session of [game]... I often found myself wishing I could do something else.
In my most recent session of [game]... I felt that I made progress while playing.
In my most recent session of [game]... I felt disappointed with my performance.
In my most recent session of [game]... I felt I formed relationships with other players and/or characters.
In my most recent session of [game]... Interactions with other players and/or characters felt toxic to me.

tables.name: ballou_2025_bpnsfs
tables.instrument: Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale (BPNSFS), brief daily version
tables.description: Daily diary (US participants, 30 days): one BPNSFS item for each of autonomy, competence and relatedness satisfaction and frustration, about the day. 1 = very strongly disagree .. 7 = very strongly agree.
tables.dict_note: Sparse per person: the median person answers each item 8 times (interquartile range 2 to 23), because most people completed only a few of the 30 daily surveys. These are short diaries for most people, not a dense diary.

items.stem: The next statements tap into your experiences today. Please indicate for each of the statements to what extent they are true for you.Today... ... I was able to do things that I really want and value in life.
items.construct: autonomy, self-determination, need satisfaction, basic psychological needs

items.stem: The next statements tap into your experiences today. Please indicate for each of the statements to what extent they are true for you.Today... ... I felt forced to do many things I wouldn’t choose to do.
items.construct: self-determination, need frustration, basic psychological needs

items.stem: The next statements tap into your experiences today. Please indicate for each of the statements to what extent they are true for you.Today... ... I could do things well and achieve my goals.
items.construct: competence, need satisfaction, competence satisfaction, mastery, self-efficacy, basic psychological needs

items.stem: The next statements tap into your experiences today. Please indicate for each of the statements to what extent they are true for you.Today... ... I felt insecure about my abilities.
items.construct: competence, need satisfaction, competence satisfaction, insecurity, self-efficacy, basic psychological needs

items.stem: The next statements tap into your experiences today. Please indicate for each of the statements to what extent they are true for you.Today... ... I felt close and connected with other people whom I care about and who care about me.
items.construct: relatedness, social connectedness, need satisfaction, basic psychological needs

items.stem: The next statements tap into your experiences today. Please indicate for each of the statements to what extent they are true for you.Today... ... I felt excluded from the group I want to belong to.
items.construct: relatedness, social connectedness, social exclusion, need satisfaction, basic psychological needs

itemtext.why: Left off for this PR, per #3421.

notes: 17 people (68 rows) are dropped (EXCLUDE_IDS). openESM built its copy on 2026-07-22 from open-play v1.2.3; open-play v1.3.0 (2026-10-16) 'corrected participant qualification' and 'fixed partial-survey-response filtering', and these 17 are not in its survey_daily: 12 are gone from the release, 3 are qualified=FALSE in its intake, 2 are qualified but filtered out. Every shipped value in the remaining rows matches v1.3.0 where rows match on id and time stamp.

For the openESM report (#1698): 0075_ballou predates open-play v1.3.0, which removed 17 of its people (68 rows) as unqualified or partial; and openESM types `date` as Date although it holds full ISO time stamps.
The deposit's BANGS items carry the lead-in 'In my most recent session of [game]...' (codebook.xlsx, Daily tab); openESM's wording omits it. The stems here include it.

bpnsfs_dup_item / bpnsfs_dup_score repeat one BPNSFS item as a consistency check (v2 preprint, data quality, says BANGS; the data say BPNSFS). Not shipped: it duplicates an item already in the table, and no row fails the check (bpnsfs_failed_att_check is FALSE throughout).

flags.what: no time stamps or counter: `wave` = (day - day_min) * beeps_per_day + (beep - beep_min) + 1. Check beeps_per_day against the sampling scheme ('1x/day at 2 pm local time'); no `date`.
flags.resolution: wave = each person's daily surveys numbered in time order of date; date = that stamp in Unix seconds, true UTC (see date.tz_evidence). openESM types date as Date, so plan proposed day/beep, but the column holds full time stamps. openESM's day agrees with time order for every survey; no stamp is missing or repeated; beep is always 1 (one survey a day). No source states the collection period, so the date window is the data's own span.

flags.what: 1 proposed table(s) hold a single item (ballou_2025_sleep_quality). Decide for each whether it belongs with a neighbouring table of the same questionnaire, stands alone, or is not shipped.
flags.resolution: sleep_quality is not shipped: a single 1-5 item, and the 3-item floor bars merging it with unrelated items (datastandard.md).

flags.what: Tables are a first guess from file order, response scale, source, prompts asked at, and column-name prefixes. Read the codebook and split or merge so each table is one instrument or subscale (datastandard.md, 'One file per scale'); rename each `<author>_<year>_<construct>`, and set `script` to the record's name.
flags.resolution: Two tables, one per instrument (codebook.xlsx, Daily tab): ballou_2025_bangs, the six BANGS items about the most recent gaming session, and ballou_2025_bpnsfs, the six brief BPNSFS items about the day. The seven how_stressful_* ratings are not shipped: each rates a different event type and is asked only when that event was ticked, so they are not one scale.

flags.what: `candidates` holds columns that may or may not be items (binary checkboxes, counts, rating scales whose coding gives no anchors -- affective_valence, life_satisfaction). Move any that are responses into a table; the rest go to `not_shipped` with a reason. played24hr, had_stress, affective_valence, life_satisfaction
flags.resolution: played24hr and had_stress are routing questions; affective_valence and life_satisfaction are single 0-100 sliders under the 3-item floor. All four go to not_shipped.

flags.what: openESM says cross-sectional (baseline) data exist. Covariates such as age and gender are not handled by this tool: add them by hand to the generated script if wanted (neubauer_2023_stecco does), or note why not.
flags.resolution: No covariates. openESM's copy carries none; age, gender and country are in the deposit's survey_intake file, whose participant set has moved on from openESM's snapshot, and the licence's no-reidentification clause argues against adding demographics that nothing here needs.

flags.what: Read openESM's additional_comments: 'Part of the "open play" project; more video game and time use data and additional surveys available on Zenodo and GitHub (https://github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play). Find the modified license on GitHub and Zenodo.'
flags.resolution: Read. The modified licence is handled under the licence flag. The biweekly surveys, intake and telemetry in the open-play deposit are not in openESM's copy and are out of scope for this record.

flags.what: Licence: openESM 'CC0 1.0 - modified'; original deposit 'TODO' (not OSF or Zenodo; read https://github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play/tree/main/data). IRW carries openESM's label when it is stricter (ruled 2026-10-04); if the two differ, the difference goes in the notes and in the report to openESM.
flags.resolution: openESM labels the copy 'CC0 1.0 - modified'; the original deposit's LICENSE is CC0 1.0 with an added no-reidentification clause (section 5). Cleared on #3421 (2026-11-15): carried as CC0 1.0, with the clause in the dictionary notes.

flags.what: `reference` is drafted from openESM's BibTeX. Check it against the paper's DOI: the year (online vs print), page range and author list are where it goes wrong.
flags.resolution: openESM's BibTeX is an @online entry, so the draft lost the title. The deposit's CITATION.cff cites the dataset only (v1.2.7, no paper), so the reference is the current PsyArXiv version, v2 (10.31234/osf.io/nz96c_v2, posted 2026-09-09); openESM cites v1. No journal version yet.

flags.what: openESM's copy (built 2026-07-22 from open-play v1.2.3) predates open-play v1.3.0 (2026-10-16); 17 people (68 rows) in it are not in v1.3.0's survey_daily.
flags.resolution: Dropped via exclude_ids: the authors' own v1.3.0 release removed them (corrected participant qualification, partial-response filtering). See the coding notes; reported to openESM (#1698).
